html:
The Tuyuca, who call themselves Dokapuara, are an Eastern Tukanoan people of the Vaupés region on the border of Colombia and Brazil, on the Tiquié and Papurí rivers.

Like their neighbours, they follow the Vaupés custom of marrying outside one's own language group, so households are multilingual. The Tuyuca language is known to linguists for its evidentials: endings on every statement that show how the speaker knows it, whether seen, heard, inferred or told. Neighbours include the Barasano, the Tatuyo, the Wanano and the Arawakan Tariana. See also Tucanoan languages.
